posts.caption: Red's day starts at 5:50, when the first truck pulls into the lot. By 5:51 she's at the stall door inspecting the driveway. After breakfast she posts herself at the end of the aisle and watches the barn cat make his rounds. At noon she checks the hay. At four she reviews the water. The boarders think I'm exaggerating until they've spent a full day out here. After that they say good morning to her first. It took the vet three visits to work out whose barn this is.
posts.first: I used to apologize for how much room she takes up. Now I just move the wheelbarrow. She has never stepped on my foot on purpose, and I keep a short list of the times it was an accident. It's shorter than it should be, honestly. She's careful where it counts.

posts.caption: One morning I found the feed room door latched and the window above the grain bin open about eight inches. Pudding was standing on a mounting block that had been twenty feet away the night before. There was a very small amount of sweet feed on his nose and a great deal of calm on his face. I closed the window, moved the block, and added a second latch. He watched me do all of it like a man reading the terms and conditions. I should have known by the way he blinked.
posts.first: The second latch lasted nine days. I stopped asking how and started keeping the grain in the truck. Now he stands near the truck every morning at six, not doing anything, in a very casual way. I have never met anyone who looks so little like a criminal.

posts.quote: A new blanket fits perfectly for exactly one week. After that, the horse grows a winter coat and a new opinion.
posts.first: I've bought six blankets in eleven years and each one fit for about a week. The tags say 'adjustable.' So far that has only described me. I stand in the aisle with a buckle in each hand and the horse stands there looking rounder, and we both agree it's the blanket's fault.

posts.caption: My husband keeps a spreadsheet for the horse. It has columns for hay, shavings, farrier and vet, plus a tab labeled Misc that has grown every year since 2019. He reads it aloud at the kitchen table in the voice of a man delivering the weather. Then he finishes his coffee, puts on his boots, and walks out to the barn without a word. The spreadsheet gets updated on the first of the month. The barn gets visited twice a day. The Misc tab now has its own Misc tab.
posts.first: He asked me last spring if we could cut back on something, and I said we could cut back on the spreadsheet. He thought that was funny for about a week. Then he printed it and put it in a folder. It's labeled 'Horse,' which I think says it all.

posts.caption: The feed truck is supposed to arrive between nine and noon, which at our barn means eleven forty. The old gelding stands at the paddock fence from nine, facing the driveway, without any visible concern. The young horses pace and whinny and check the road every four minutes. He just leans on the post. When the truck finally turns in, he lifts his head about an inch. That's the entire reaction. I've learned more about patience from him than from any book on my shelf, and I own several.
posts.first: He's twenty-six now and I'm fifty-eight, and we've both settled into waiting for the truck. His method is better. I check my phone and he checks nothing. In all these years he has never once been wrong about when it was coming.

posts.caption: The vet came out for fall shots and the Diva spent the morning getting ready like it was a gala. I braided her forelock, polished the buckles, and picked out the good lead rope. She stood in the wash rack with her chin up while he worked. He gave her one shot, wrote on his clipboard, and told me she was in great shape. He said nothing about the braid. She noticed. She's been sulking at the gate since four. Next time I'm bringing a bow.
posts.first: She kept the good halter on all day and wouldn't let me take it off until supper. I think she wanted it on in case anyone came by to say something. Nobody did. The barn cat said nothing either, and she holds that against him too.
